scope_depth_review.budget_result: Within the assigned 1,400–1,700-word and six-primary-URL limits.
scope_depth_review.coverage: Answers the finite Ampere 2:4 question across hardware eligibility, compressed representation, A100 peak rates, sampled INT8 GEMM behavior, TensorRT 8.0 A100 network evidence, pruning quality, conversion boundary, and dense-selected tactics. It includes a favorable network case, an unfavorable MobileNet quality case before channel permutation, and a hypothesis-only portability checklist.

The post does not publish per-batch latency, repetitions, clocks, or tactic logs; the GEMM paper does not give a universal crossover. The report states these boundaries and does not infer an Arc result.

primary_source_audit.title: NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU Architecture In-Depth
primary_source_audit.verified_version: Official whitepaper V1.0; title page labels the A100 Tensor Core GPU Architecture.
primary_source_audit.audit: Supports the A100 2:4 pattern, compressed storage, skipped-zero Sparse MMA, and the illustrative N versus N/2 cycle example. The report correctly treats 2x as an eligible-operation ceiling rather than a network multiplier.

primary_source_audit.title: Accelerating Sparse Deep Neural Networks
primary_source_audit.audit: Primary paper confirms 16-bit/INT8 peak rates, TF32's 1:2 pattern, metadata and storage arithmetic, dimension multiples as stated by the paper, cuSPARSELt-versus-cuBLAS GEMM comparison, N=10K at sequence 256 and batch 40, pruning/retraining, and the cited ResNet-50/MobileNet v2 accuracy examples.

primary_source_audit.title: Accelerating Inference with Sparsity Using the NVIDIA Ampere Architecture and NVIDIA TensorRT
primary_source_audit.verified_version: NVIDIA Technical Blog, 2021-07-20; describes TensorRT 8.0 and A100 FP16 measurements.
primary_source_audit.audit: Confirms ResNeXt-101_32x8d ImageNet Top-1 of 79.3 for both dense and sparse FP16. Vendor prose says performance approaches 20% at larger batch sizes and performance per watt reaches 36% at smaller batches. The report's 1.10–1.18 and per-batch efficiency figures are chart read-offs and are correctly marked approximate, but its short-answer 10–18% range could be mistaken for the vendor's stated maximum; preserve the distinction in R886-C2.

primary_source_audit.title: TensorRT structured sparsity documentation
primary_source_audit.verified_current_version: TensorRT 11.4.0 is listed as latest; page title is Data Formats and Tensors, sparsity section last updated 2026-10-05.
primary_source_audit.verified_versioned_10x_metadata: Archived reference page; it lists 10.16.1 as latest within 10.x and says last updated 2026-05-23. Its heading is I/O Formats, with sparsity as a section. The report's /10.16.1/ URL returns 404.
primary_source_audit.audit: The current 11.4 page independently confirms the 2:4 convolution and MatrixMultiply checks, FP16/INT8 enablement, and that eligible layers may retain dense tactics; its example says 53 layers eligible and 22 chose sparse tactics. The 10.x archive retains the old 3-eligible/2-selected log. Neither example gives device, batch, layer shapes, latency, or accuracy.

corrections.finding: R4's literal /10.16.1/ URL is dead, its page title/version date are inaccurate, and the report calls an archived TensorRT 10.x page current even though TensorRT 11.4.0 is current on 2026-10-16.
corrections.action: For current behavior, cite the verified 11.4.0 Data Formats and Tensors URL and record its sparsity section/date. If retaining the TensorRT 10.16.1 counterexample specifically, link the /10.x.x/ archived page, label it archived, use the I/O Formats title, and correct the page update date to 2026-05-23. The 10.x example remains valid as version-scoped documentation, not as current-version evidence.

corrections.finding: The blog's own prose says performance is approaching 20% at large batch sizes; the 18% upper value is a visual chart estimate, not its reported maximum or raw measurement.
corrections.action: Keep per-batch values labeled approximate chart read-offs. When summarizing the vendor's stated maximum, report 'approaching 20%' and retain the separate 'up to 36% performance per watt at smaller batch sizes' claim. Do not infer precise latencies or a timing boundary absent from the post.
